body.statement:
Fix the declared regime constants.  Does there exist a constant \(c>0\) such that, for every admissible deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) for which \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\lambda\) for some \(\lambda\in[0,\infty]\), there exists a deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, allowed to depend on the entire threshold sequence but not on the realized data, with the following properties?  For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be exactly the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) of \(\texttt{def:total-gram-estimator}\) formed with the three blocks in \(B_n\), and interpret the design argument of \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}\) as the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\), using the third block in \(B_n\).  Put
\[
 R_{n,B_n}(z)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha),
 \qquad
 t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},
\]
and define the explicit candidate interval
\[
 C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)=
 \left[
 \max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
 \min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Is this interval eventually uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest, in the sense that
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P^{\otimes n}
 \left\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), while retaining bounded \(Y\) and the measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\)?  If
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
 =\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
 \left[\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)\right],
\]
do both sharp-constant limits
\[
 \frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\longrightarrow c,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{r_n}\longrightarrow c
\]
hold?  Finally, writing \(W_{n,B_n}=\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\) for the worst integrated radius computed with the third block in \(B_n\), is there a least-favorable mixed regular-plus-local pair with target separation \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\) such that
\[
 \frac{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{2W_{n,B_n}}{L_n^\star}\longrightarrow1?
\]
Here \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius, so \(2W_{n,B_n}\) is the candidate untruncated expected full length.  The convention \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)=0\) when the affine feasible set is empty remains in force.  This question does not assert that the zero-totalized candidate is honest, nondegenerate, or optimal.
body.justification: The question now names one fully explicit candidate: a deterministic admissible split sequence, the total-Gram center, and the exact realized-modulus radius.  This makes coverage, expected full length, and the proposed sharp constant properties mathematically auditable for a single sample map.
body.gap: The proved order bounds do not select a deterministic split sequence or establish a joint sharp limit experiment.  Fixed-design convex-modulus theory also does not settle uniform honesty of the zero-totalized radius, the moving random design under a merely measurable polynomial density envelope, or the three mixed regular-plus-local matching limits.
body.consumer: A positive resolution would calibrate the shortest defensible full-length interval for a future atom-aware implementation of the same lower-threshold policy specification; a negative resolution would reject this explicit split-selected, total-Gram-centered candidate rather than the proved order-optimal interval.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether there exist a common sharp constant \(c>0\) and, for every admissible threshold sequence with a finite or infinite critical-scale limit, a deterministic data-independent split sequence \(B_{\bullet}\) for which the explicit total-Gram-centered modulus interval is eventually uniformly honest and satisfies all three mixed-experiment matching limits.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen results prove only \(L_n^\star\asymp r_n\) and order-optimal honesty for the different bias-aware fallback interval.  They do not provide the joint local asymptotic experiment, exact minimax constant, uniform integrability of the literal real-valued modulus handle in every higher-order regime, or a proof that zero radius on affine-infeasible designs preserves coverage.
obligation.attempted: The order-optimal upper and lower constructions, the phase decomposition, and the exact realized-design modulus definition were compared.  They control rates but do not identify a common constant or certify the explicit modulus candidate's coverage; promoting any of those missing properties to an assumption would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: Theorems \(\texttt{thm:honest-length}\) and \(\texttt{thm:phase-diagram}\) establish \(c r_n\leq L_n^\star\leq C r_n\) uniformly across the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes, and an explicit bias-aware atom-fallback interval attains the upper order.
